I rendered PDF page 4 to PNG (page render, 100 dpi) and read the image: under the bold heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' the single line reads exactly 'The stress is predictably on the first syllable. All five vowels occur both short and long.' Verbatim confirmed. I also re-decoded the text layer independently: the body text is shifted -1 codepoint in the raw extraction (raw 'Sgd rsqdrr hr oqdchbs`akx nm sgd ehqrs rxkk`akd- @kk ehud unvdkr nbbtq ansg rgnqs `mc knmf-' -> +1 = the sentence above), while headings extract unshifted; the other read…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and falls on the first syllable of the word. Vowel length is phonemic (five short vs. five long vowels) and is treated separately from stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement in a one-sentence suprasegmentals note of a 6-page SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet; no examples with stress marked, no discussion of phrase-level prominence or of long-vowel interaction with stress. The OPD sheet is the standardized summary of Olkkonen's 2000 'Borong (Kosorong) phonology' manuscript (cited in its bibliography), which was not located.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD's title, language code [KSR], location (between Mindik and Pindiu, Morobe), villages (Ebebang, Hamoronong) and the recorded text are Borong/Kosorong = boro1279; but its running page header on pp. 2-6 reads 'Burum-Mindik [Mindik dialect] (Somba-Siawari) OPD', a template artifact from the Olkkonens' primary language Somba-Siawari (Burum-Mindik), and the PDF metadata title is 'Borong-Kosorong_ksr.rtf'. Dialect not specified (Ethnologue/IEL list Kosorong and Yangeborong dialects); the data appear to be from the Kosorong (Ebebang) area. Glottolog's 6-page 'Borong organised phonology data' (Olkkonen 2001, ref 20563) matches this sheet ('Data checked by: Soini Olkkonen (2001)').
